claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and have not undergone prior thermal treatment.
Surface segregation of Cu governs the onset of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Segregated Cu forms a Cu-enriched, liquid-like premelting film at the nanoparticle surface.
The Cu-enriched premelting film destabilizes the neighboring solid lattice.
The surface premelting film nucleates the overall phase transition.
Cu has the lowest melting temperature among the components of the FeNiCrCoCu alloy.
Near the nanoparticle melting point, Cu segregates to the surface.
The Cu-enriched liquid-like film lowers the effective energy barrier for the phase transition.
An inert amorphous-carbon coating suppresses surface diffusion.
Suppression of surface diffusion by the coating delays formation of the Cu-enriched premelting film.
Delayed formation of the premelting film shifts the onset of premelting to a higher temperature.
Bare and amorphous-carbon-coated nanoparticles should be compared under identical heating rates and ambient conditions.
Uncoated nanoparticles should show surface-premelting signatures at lower temperatures than coated nanoparticles.
Changes in TEM contrast can indicate surface premelting.
Shifts in diffraction patterns or diffuse scattering can indicate premelting.
Earlier premelting in uncoated particles should coincide with a higher surface Cu concentration.
Under high-vacuum or low-oxygen conditions near the expected Cu-related melting onset, surface diffusion is the primary variable affecting premelting onset.
The carbon coating may alter TEM contrast, interfacial stress, or other interfacial properties.
Failure of uncoated particles to premelt earlier than coated particles would falsify the proposed control by surface Cu segregation.
Failure to observe greater Cu surface segregation in uncoated particles would falsify the proposed mechanism.
